Visit note | 2025-08-06 10:00 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Anwar Chowdhury, 66, male. Mr. Chowdhury reports experiencing wheezing on walking, a long history of smoking, and breathlessness that has been worse for several days. He mentions his symptoms worsened during the dusty dry season in Chattogram. He works as a tailor and has smoked for decades. He has a known comorbidity of Essential hypertension. He denies any chest pain at rest or ankle swelling. On examination: SpO2 89%, BP 151/90 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 59 kg. Chest examination reveals diffuse expiratory wheezes and decreased breath sounds bilaterally. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-08-06 10:30 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Habiba Uddin, 24, female. On examination: temperature 99.6°F, BP 150/90 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, SpO2 95%, weight 50 kg. Lungs show clear vesicular breath sounds with scattered rhonchi. Assessment: Acute bronchitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink warm fluids, use steam inhalation twice daily, and avoid smoke. Follow-up in 2 weeks if the cough continues.

Visit note | 2025-08-06 11:00 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Sharmin Siddique, 44, female. Mrs. Siddique reports suffering from severe aching in the bones and muscles and a sudden high fever. She states the illness started after a week of stagnant rainwater around the house in Bogura. She works as a beautician and has a background of Hypothyroidism. She denies rash or respiratory symptoms. On examination: platelet count 133000 per microlitre, temperature 101.1°F, BP 127/72 mmHg, pulse 101 bpm, weight 66 kg. General survey shows febrile appearance with mild myalgia. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-08-06 11:00 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Riad Rahman, 41, male. Mr. Rahman presents with complaints of a brief spinning sensation when turning in bed and dizziness when looking up. He explains that these symptoms began after a viral cold in Tangail. He works as a bus driver, spending long hours navigating traffic, and reports no previous neurological issues or chronic medical conditions. He denies headache, visual changes, weakness, or numbness in his limbs. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the left side, BP 117/84 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, weight 56 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and cerebellar tests are normal. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued to help manage the dizzy spells. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
